title: Sampler-driven kernel aggregation with NVTX context and decode-prefill epoch markers
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Goal: produce a low-overhead, queryable surface of per-kernel performance at phase granularity (prefill vs decode) by combining light-weight sampling, NVTX range context, and explicit epoch markers. This ticket delivers: (1) a sampled aggregator that attaches kernel attribution to sampled spans; (2) deterministic epoch markers emitted at phase boundaries so traces and metrics can be grouped by prefill/decode windows; and (3) an ingestion schema and dashboard for aggregate views (latency distributions, tail percentiles, kernel hotspot fingerprints).

Motivation: existing telemetry gives raw kernel timings and NVTX ranges but lacks a robust way to attribute noisy kernel records to logical prefill/decode epochs and to compute stable aggregated distributions without exploding cardinality or cost. Full per-request tracing for every token is too expensive at production QPS. A sampler-driven approach lets us get statistically meaningful histograms while keeping overhead minimal.

Design summary:
- Epoch markers: runtime emits immutable epoch_id NVTX ranges at the start/end of prefill and decode phases for each request. Epochs are hierarchical: request_id -> epoch_id (prefill/first-decode/continued-decode). They are emitted as NVTX push/pop pairs with a short fixed tag ("epoch-v1").
- Sampler: a probabilistic request sampler (configurable via console; default 0.5%) will trace a subset of requests with full per-kernel timing, NVTX envelope, and kernel fingerprint metadata. Sampler decisions are sticky for a request lifetime.
- Kernel attribution: sampled spans will include per-kernel annotations (kernel_name, kernel_variant, workspace_id, seq_len, batch_size, kernel_ms). We attach the current epoch_id to each span by reading active NVTX context at kernel entry. For non-sampled requests we emit compact per-kernel counters aggregated by epoch bucket using an edge-case fast-path (approximate counters, no span).
- Aggregation and retention: sampler payloads are ingested into the profiling pipeline (OTLP->collector->clickhouse). Aggregation jobs compute epoch-scoped histograms (p50/p95/p99), kernel hotspot lists, and per-configuration deltas (quantization, kernel selection). Retain raw sampled traces 30d, aggregated histograms 180d.

Trade-offs considered:
- Sampling rate vs visibility: higher rate gives better tail estimates but higher cost and potential CPU overhead in the runtime. We'll expose sampling rate per customer tier with conservative defaults for hosted.
- NVTX envelope cost: pushing epoch NVTX ranges adds a few microseconds; we keep tag strings short and only emit markers at phase boundaries.
- Cardinality: adding epoch_id to kernel attribution can raise cardinality if we attach many other dimensions (exact seq_len, model_version). We mitigate by bucketing seq_len and model_version to coarse bins in the aggregation pipeline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits epoch NVTX markers and sampled spans in canary build.
- Sampler end-to-end verified: traces show kernel timings with epoch_id and kernel_fingerprint for sampled requests at canary QPS without exceeding CPU overhead budget (<= 1% p95 latency regression on canary).
- Aggregation pipeline populates dashboard with per-epoch histograms and kernel hotspot ranking for the canary tenant.
- New dashboard has filters for model, quantization profile, epoch (prefill/first-decode/continued-decode), and sampling cohort.

Observability & validation plan:
- Add synthetic load test that simulates common seq_len distributions and measures histogram convergence vs sampling rate.
- Side-by-side comparison: run full tracing for a short window (test cluster) to validate sampled estimates against ground truth.
- Monitor runtime CPU cost, trace ingestion volume, and ClickHouse storage delta during canary.

Implementation notes and links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Sampler-driven+kernel+aggregation+design
- Draft schema: https://go.redwood.ai/schemas/profiling/epoch-v1 (internal schema doc)
- Dashboard prototype: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/rt-kernel-epoch/profiling-overview
- Proof-of-concept branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893

Next steps:
1) Land epoch marker NVTX push/pop (runtime change) and a lightweight API to read current epoch in kernel wrapper. (owner: Sofia)
2) Implement sampler decision and span emission path. (owner: Sofia)
3) Add aggregation job and dashboard widgets. (owner: Observability eng)
4) Canary with two internal tenants, measure overhead and sampling accuracy.

Longer term: integrate kernel fingerprinting (hash of opcode pattern + config) to de-duplicate noisy kernel names and enable regression alerts tied to kernel-level performance shifts.
acceptance_criteria: Epoch NVTX markers emitted at phase boundaries in canary runtime
Sampled spans include kernel_name, kernel_variant, kernel_ms, and epoch_id
Histogram aggregation pipeline produces p50/p95/p99 per-epoch per-kernel
Canary CPU overhead < 1% p95 latency regression
Dashboard filters and charts online for canary tenants
comments: 2025-01-14 Marco Rivera: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed on epoch marker format and default sampling rate of 0.5%. Agreed to bucket seq_len into {short:<128, medium:128-512, long:>512} for aggregation.

2025-01-21 Sofia Chen: PR 1893 created with NVTX epoch push/pop implementation and unit tests. Measuring microbenchmark overhead; preliminary shows ~1.1us per marker. Moving NVTX strings to interned ids to reduce cost.
2025-01-29 Observability Eng: Aggregation job draft ready. Using ClickHouse TTLs for retention. Need schema sign-off from infra/security for OTLP sampling export paths.
2025-02-03 QA: Synthetic convergence test added — at 0.5% sampling rate, p95 estimate error < 7% for kernels with >200K ops/day. Edge cases for rare kernels flagged for increased sampling cohort.

2025-02-05 Sofia Chen: Canary started on two internal tenants (east/central). Initial ingestion volume +12% and CPU delta ~0.6% for canary hosts. No visible tail regressions in the first 24h. Moving to broader canary next week.
